Q: Multiple dynamic arrays with arena memory allocator when parsing glTF A:

  1. Two-Pass Parsing: Scan the JSON string once to count elements, allocate the exact size in the arena, then scan a second time to parse the data.

  2. Double-Ended Arena: Allocate permanent data from the bottom up, and temporary growing arrays from the top down. Once an array finishes growing, copy it to the permanent bottom and reset the top pointer.

  3. Arena Dead Zones: Use standard arena reallocation. If an array needs to grow and isn't the newest allocation, copy it to the end of the arena and accept the old memory block as wasted space.

Q: Set Sharepoint site header background image via API A:

You can use the setsitelogo method in a Send an HTTP request to SharePoint action, if it site based on a Team site template. You can host the background image in your Site Assets library and use a relativeLogoUrl.

Below is an example, if that helps?

URI

_api/siteiconmanager/setsitelogo

Body

{
    "relativeLogoUrl": "%2Fsites%2FChangetheLook-TeamSite%2FSiteAssets%2Fexamplebackground.png",
    "type": 2,
    "aspect": 0
}

Q: Find and remove the out-of-order numeric element in a vector A:

For each input vector decide if it is approximately increasing or decreasing by checking the number of positive vs negative successive differences. If there are more positive differences assume increasing else decreasing. If decreasing negate all values converting it to the increasing case so that we only have to consider that case.

Then using integer linear programming with the CVXR package assign a boolean b[i] to the i-th component in the input vector. b[i] is 1 if we keep that component and 0 if we drop it. We want the longest vector possible so our objective is to maximize sum(b) over all b subject to the following constraints. For each pair i < j if x[i] > x[j] then our increasing condition is violated so we add a constraint which prevents both positions, i and j, from being kept. Both can be zero or one of them can be one but they cannot both be one. Such a constraint is b[i] + b[j] <= 1. We now have an objective and a set of constraints forming an integer linear program which we solve.

Now we want to exclude any solution which is not unique. To do that we add two conditions. If the objective function in the solution above was K and b' is the solution to the second problem then we must ensure that sum(b') is also K or else it is not as good a solution as the first. Also we must ensure that b' is not the same as b. We can do that by requiring that the sum of the b'[i] over those i for which b[i] = 1 is less than K. If this second integer linear program has a solution then the solutions are not unique so we return the input; otherwise, the first problem gave a unique solution so we return it.

library(CVXR)

solve_ilp <- function(target_vec, K = NULL, x_cut = NULL) {
  n <- length(target_vec)
  x <- Variable(n, boolean = TRUE)
  constraints <- list()
  for (i in 1:n) {
    for (j in 1:n) {
      if (i >= j) next
      if (target_vec[i] >= target_vec[j]) {
        constraints <- c(constraints, list(x[i] + x[j] <= 1))
      } } }
  if (!is.null(K) && !is.null(x_cut)) {
    constraints <- c(constraints, list(sum(x) == K, sum(x[x_cut == 1]) <= K - 1))
  }
  objective <- Maximize(sum(x))
  prob <- Problem(objective, constraints)
  psolve(prob)
  list(prob = prob, x = x)
}

apply_rules <- function(vec) {
  n <- length(vec)
  if (n < 2) return(vec)
  diffs <- diff(vec)
  is_rising <- sum(diffs > 0) > (length(diffs) / 2)
  target_vec <- if (is_rising) vec else -vec
  step1 <- solve_ilp(target_vec)
  if (status(step1$prob) != "optimal") return(vec)
  x_star <- round(value(step1$x))
  K <- sum(x_star)
  step2 <- solve_ilp(target_vec, K = K, x_cut = x_star)
  if (status(step2$prob) == "infeasible") vec[x_star == 1] else vec
}

Q: Eclipse&Maven - The import org.hibernate.boot.cannot be resolved A:

It could be because of the broken classpath;

Package explorer > Plug-in tools > Update classpath.

Or your Hibernate jar is not well extracted from the zip file. For controll, from Project Explorer try to expand your Hibernate jar. If you can't expand probably it's corrupted. Try to add jar again.
